assignments.name: prompt_item
assignments.value:
You are an AI product analyst helping a product manager track releases from AI companies. You will get one item with a title, date, link and text.

Rules:
- Use ONLY the text given. Do not invent facts, prices, dates or model names.
- If the text does not say enough, say so in so_what and set impact to Low.
- Write short sentences in plain English.
- Do not use em-dashes.

Return ONLY a JSON object. No markdown, no extra text. Keys:
category: one of Model Release, Pricing and Limits, Deprecation, New Feature, Policy and Safety, Dev Tooling, Other
pm_lens: one of Build, Cost, Risk, Compete, Users
  (Build = a new capability a PM could ship. Cost = changes unit economics or rate limits. Risk = breaking change, deprecation or policy shift. Compete = closes a gap or creates differentiation. Users = changes what users will expect.)
urgency: one of Act now, Plan this quarter, Watch
impact: one of High, Medium, Low
summary: max 25 words
so_what: one sentence on why this matters to a PM
action: one short suggested next step for a PM

assignments.name: prompt_brief
assignments.value:
You write a weekly brief for an AI Product Manager. You get a JSON list of analysed items from this week.

Rules:
- Use only that data. Never invent items, facts or links. Use each link exactly as given.
- Do not invent personal experiences or claim anything was tested.
- Do not use em-dashes, en-dashes or emojis.
- Keep the whole brief under 2,800 characters including links and hashtags.
- Write each link as plain text. No bold, no brackets, no markdown around links.
- Mention exactly 5 items (or all items if fewer than 5 exist) and link only to those. Never list or link to any other item.

Voice (match this):
- Open with one plain line telling what the brief covers. No greeting, no hype.
- Short lines. Use the arrow symbol → for points.
- Simple words, like explaining to a smart colleague who is new to AI.

Structure:
1. Opening line mentioning the intent of the brief
2. Exactly 5 items (fewer only if fewer exist), ranked by impact and urgency. For each: company and what changed, why it matters to PMs, then the link. Do not mention any other item.
3. One line on which PM lens (Build, Cost, Risk, Compete, Users) showed up most this week.
4. Do not include hashtags.

parameters.content:
SETTINGS
Edit the Settings node to change lookback days, email, limits, boost and demote keywords and prompts. Nothing else needs touching.

TEST MODES
Manual run = test. Set test_source to samples (no feeds, no waiting) or feeds (real feeds, 30 day lookback). Scheduled run = live. Hover over correct trigger and click execute workflow.

ADD AN AI PRODUCT THAT YOU NEED YOUR EYES ON
Open the sources data table and add a row: company, name, RSS url, enabled = true. No workflow change needed.

SWITCH LLM
Change llm_base_url and llm_model in Settings, then put the new key in the LLM API Key credential.

assignments.name: corpus
assignments.value: ={{ $('Cap Items').all().map(i => (i.json.title + ' ' + i.json.snippet)).join(' ') + ' ' + $('Pack Items').first().json.items.map(i => i.summary + ' ' + i.so_what + ' ' + i.action).join(' ') }}

assignments.name: chk_tags_valid
assignments.value: ={{ $('Pack Items').first().json.items.every(i => ['Model Release','Pricing and Limits','Deprecation','New Feature','Policy and Safety','Dev Tooling','Other'].includes(i.category) && ['Build','Cost','Risk','Compete','Users'].includes(i.pm_lens) && ['Act now','Plan this quarter','Watch'].includes(i.urgency) && ['High','Medium','Low'].includes(i.impact)) }}

assignments.name: checks_report
assignments.value: ={{ [["Brief under 3000 characters", $json.chk_length], ["No em-dashes or en-dashes", $json.chk_no_dashes], ["No hashtags", $json.chk_no_hashtags], ["Every link in the brief is a real fetched link", $json.chk_links_real], ["Brief covers 5 items or fewer", $json.chk_top5], ["All tags use allowed values", $json.chk_tags_valid], ["Every item has summary, so-what and action", $json.chk_fields_filled], ["No duplicate items", $json.chk_no_dup_links], ["Every selected item was analysed", $json.chk_all_processed]].map(c => (c[1] ? 'PASS    ' : 'FAIL    ') + c[0]).join('\n') + '\n' + ($json.chk_numbers_grounded ? 'PASS    ' : 'REVIEW  ') + 'Numbers in the brief appear in the source text (can false-alarm, check by eye)' }}

assignments.name: score
assignments.value: ={{ Math.max(0, Math.min(30, $('Settings').first().json.boost_keywords.split(',').map(k => k.trim()).filter(k => k).reduce((n, k) => n + (new RegExp('\\b' + k, 'i').test($json.title || '') ? 3 : 0) + (new RegExp('\\b' + k, 'i').test($json.snippet || '') ? 1 : 0), 0) - $('Settings').first().json.demote_keywords.split(',').map(k => k.trim()).filter(k => k).reduce((n, k) => n + (new RegExp('\\b' + k, 'i').test($json.title || '') ? 5 : 0), 0))) }}

parameters.content:
ADD A DETERMINISTIC CHECK HERE
LLM based evals are out of scope for this workflow currently

## Workflow Overview
Purpose- To analyze and create a brief of recent AI Product Releases with a PM lens to be able to plan and take decisions
Trigger source-Schedule or Manual
Input format- Website links
Output format- Brief delivered over email
Pre-requisite- One time setup for log and source tables (separate workflow) 
Error handling strategy- Deterministic checks (in this workflow) and separate error workflow (both reported over email)
Owner-
Gives each item points for boost words and subtracts points for demote words
Orders items within each company by score, then by date
Keeps only the top 10 per company, so one busy feed can’t crowd out the others.

Why not agent node and just HTTP node?
Cheaper (often free)
Faster
More deterministic
No memory required
No tool calling required
